Every converted chapter in [*ggplot2: field manual*](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/fm-ggp2/) uses simulated data with a late 90s theme, and each dataset gets a `ggplot2` theme to match. This vignette shows each theme with the data from the chapter that introduced it.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(fmggp2)
library(ggplot2)
showtext::showtext_auto()
```

## Game Boy

`theme_gameboy()` uses the four shades of green from the original Game Boy screen and the pixel font Press Start 2P, which ships with `fmggp2`. Below we simulate the starter chosen by 300 *Pokémon Red and Blue* players.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Game-Boy-FL.jpg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_gameboy/game-boy-fl.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: gameboy
set.seed(1998)
pokemon_starters <- data.frame(
  starter = sample(c("Bulbasaur", "Charmander", "Squirtle"),
    size = 300, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.30, 0.42, 0.28))
)
ggplot(pokemon_starters, aes(x = starter, fill = starter)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Pokemon Red and Blue (simulated)",
       subtitle = "Starter chosen by 300 players",
       x = "Starter", y = "Count") +
  theme_gameboy(base_size = 13)
```

## OK Soda

`theme_oksoda()` uses the gray comic book cans Coca-Cola sold from 1993 to 1995: brushed silver, black ink, OK red bars and title, and slate and brick accents, with a Courier New title. Below we simulate one day of sales at 300 test market stores from a normal distribution.

![Image: TeemPlayer, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:OK_Soda_Original_4.jpg), CC BY-SA 3.0.](../man/figures/theme_oksoda/ok-soda-original-4.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: oksoda
set.seed(1014)
ok_soda_sales <- data.frame(
  cans = round(rnorm(n = 300, mean = 45, sd = 12))
)
ggplot(ok_soda_sales, aes(x = cans)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(title = "OK Soda", caption = "Simulated data",
       subtitle = "Cans sold per store in one day",
       x = "Cans sold") +
  theme_oksoda(base_size = 13)
```

## Talkboy

`theme_talkboy()` uses the Deluxe Talkboy from *Home Alone 2* sitting on a walnut table: a silver panel, button blue marks, and a Brush Script title. Below we simulate the length of 300 recorded messages from a right skewed gamma distribution.

![Image: Y2kcrazyjoker4, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Deluxe_Talkboy_on_table.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.](../man/figures/theme_talkboy/deluxe-talkboy-on-table.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: talkboy
set.seed(1999)
talkboy_clips <- data.frame(
  seconds = round(rgamma(n = 300, shape = 4, rate = 0.5), 1)
)
ggplot(talkboy_clips, aes(x = seconds)) +
  geom_freqpoly(bins = 30) +
  labs(title = "Talkboy", caption = "Simulated data",
       subtitle = "Length of 300 recorded messages",
       x = "Message length (seconds)") +
  theme_talkboy(base_size = 13)
```

## Blockbuster

`theme_blockbuster()` uses Blockbuster Video blue and yellow. Below we simulate weekly rentals for 60 households from a Poisson distribution.

![Image: Jon Konrath from Oakland, USA, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Anchorage_Blockbuster_video_store_sign_(41219885734).jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_blockbuster/anchorage-blockbuster-video-store-sign-41219885734.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: blockbuster
set.seed(1993)
blockbuster_rentals <- data.frame(rentals = rpois(n = 60, lambda = 3))
ggplot(blockbuster_rentals, aes(x = rentals)) +
  geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, dotsize = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "Blockbuster Video (simulated)",
       x = "Number of rentals") +
  theme_blockbuster(base_size = 13)
```

## Crystal Pepsi

`theme_crystalpepsi()` uses the clear bottle and its label: a cream background, a navy frame, Pepsi red and navy marks, and a Futura title. Below we simulate the ages of 400 people at a 1992 mall taste test as a mix of kids and parents.

![Image: Mike Mozart, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Crystal_Pepsi_(29001084616).jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_crystalpepsi/crystal-pepsi-29001084616.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: crystalpepsi
set.seed(1998)
kid <- runif(400) < 0.65
tasters <- data.frame(group = ifelse(kid, "Kid", "Parent"),
  age = round(ifelse(kid, rnorm(400, 11, 2.5), rnorm(400, 37, 6))))
ggplot(tasters, aes(x = age, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 2/3) +
  labs(title = "Crystal Pepsi", caption = "Simulated data",
       x = "Age (years)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_crystalpepsi(base_size = 13)
```

## Beanie Babies

`theme_beanie()` uses a Ty heart tag red with the blanket teal and fur colors of a Beanie. Below we simulate 300 resale prices from a log normal distribution.

![Image: "[Beanie Baby](https://www.flickr.com/photos/ajay_suresh/51819429583)" by ajay_suresh, [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/).](../man/figures/theme_beanie/beanie-baby.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: beanie
set.seed(1996)
beanie_prices <- data.frame(price = rlnorm(n = 300, meanlog = log(15), sdlog = 0.8))
ggplot(beanie_prices, aes(x = "", y = price)) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(title = "Beanie Babies resale prices (simulated)",
       x = NULL, y = "Price (USD)") +
  theme_beanie(base_size = 13)
```

## Nintendo 64

`theme_n64()` uses controller gray and the four logo colors. Below we simulate 200 Mario Kart 64 lap times from a heavy tailed t distribution.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:N64-Console-Set.png), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_n64/n64-console-set.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: n64
set.seed(64)
mario_kart_laps <- data.frame(seconds = 45 + 2 * rt(n = 200, df = 3))
ggplot(mario_kart_laps, aes(x = "", y = seconds)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Mario Kart 64 (simulated)",
       x = NULL, y = "Lap time (seconds)") +
  theme_n64(base_size = 13)
```

## Jurassic Park

`theme_jurassic()` uses the Jurassic Park Post Office souvenir sheet: black, logo red, stamp yellow, and sunset orange. Below we simulate the total weight of the dinosaurs in each paddock.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jurassic_Park_icon.svg), CC0.](../man/figures/theme_jurassic/jurassic-park-icon.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: jurassic
set.seed(1993)
jp_paddocks <- data.frame(species = c("Brachiosaurus", "Triceratops", "Tyrannosaurus"),
  total_tons = c(sum(rnorm(3, 40, 5)), sum(rnorm(5, 9, 1.2)), sum(rnorm(2, 8, 1))))
ggplot(jp_paddocks, aes(x = species, y = total_tons, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Jurassic Park (simulated)", x = "Paddock", y = "Total weight (tons)") +
  theme_jurassic(base_size = 13)
```

## Happy Meals

`theme_happymeal()` uses the red and yellow of a Happy Meal box. Below we simulate average daily Happy Meal sales for four toy promotions.

![Image: Newtown grafitti from Sydney, Australia, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Happy_meal_(6955434713).jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_happymeal/happy-meal-6955434713.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: happymeal
set.seed(1997)
happy_meals <- data.frame(promotion = c("Teenie Beanie Babies", "Furby", "Hot Wheels", "Inspector Gadget"),
  avg_sold = sapply(c(420, 310, 220, 180), function(l) mean(rpois(28, l))))
ggplot(happy_meals, aes(x = promotion, y = avg_sold, fill = promotion)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Happy Meals (simulated)", x = "Toy promotion", y = "Average sold per day") +
  theme_happymeal(base_size = 13)
```

## Friends

`theme_friends()` uses Monica's apartment: purple walls, a cream sofa, a latte frame, and poppy red, navy, wood, rust, and rose marks. Below we simulate viewers per episode for three seasons.

![Image: "[Monica's Apartment, Friends](https://www.flickr.com/photos/rob-young/30987418062)" by Rob Young, [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/).](../man/figures/theme_friends/monicas-apartment.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: friends
set.seed(1994)
friends_episodes <- data.frame(season = rep(c("Season 1", "Season 3", "Season 5"), each = 24))
friends_episodes$viewers_m <- round(rnorm(72, rep(c(22, 27, 24), each = 24), 2.5))
ggplot(friends_episodes, aes(x = viewers_m, fill = season)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Friends (simulated)", x = "Viewers (millions)", y = "Episodes", fill = "Season") +
  theme_friends(base_size = 13)
```

## Fresh Prince

`theme_freshprince()` uses the logo: graffiti greens on a pink glow, and its continuous fill runs from teal to lime. Below we simulate how often the Carlton dance shows up each season.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fresh_Prince_Bel_Aire_logo.png), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_freshprince/fresh-prince-bel-aire-logo.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: freshprince
set.seed(1990)
fp <- expand.grid(season = 1:6, gag = c("Will flirts", "Carlton dance"))
fp$occurrences <- rbinom(12, 24, ifelse(fp$gag == "Will flirts", 0.9, plogis(-2.2 + 0.5 * (fp$season - 3.5))))
ggplot(fp, aes(x = season, y = gag, fill = occurrences)) +
  geom_tile() +
  labs(title = "Fresh Prince (simulated)", x = "Season", y = NULL, fill = "Episodes") +
  theme_freshprince(base_size = 13)
```

## Pogs

`theme_pogs()` uses a cardboard background and the red, sky blue, yellow, teal, purple, and rust milk cap prints. Below we simulate a collection of 100 Pogs.

![Image: "[Remember Pogs?](https://www.flickr.com/photos/mtsofan/6077181975/)" by MTSOfan, [CC BY-NC-SA 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/2.0/).](../man/figures/theme_pogs/remember-pogs.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: pogs
set.seed(1993)
pogs <- data.frame(type = sample(c("Milk caps", "Printed pogs", "Holographic", "Slammers"),
  100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.45, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10)))
ggplot(pogs, aes(x = type, fill = type)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "A Pogs collection (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Pieces") +
  theme_pogs(base_size = 13)
```

## Sony Walkman

`theme_walkman()` uses the Sports Walkman: a sports yellow body, blue buttons, a charcoal display, and an orange SPORTS label. Below we simulate median battery life for three models and two battery types.

![Image: Itsramon, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sony_Walkman02.jpg), CC BY-SA 3.0.](../man/figures/theme_walkman/sony-walkman02.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: walkman
set.seed(1979)
walkman <- data.frame(model = rep(c("WM-2", "WM-F45 Sports", "WM-EX194 Mega Bass"), times = 2),
  battery = rep(c("Alkaline", "Rechargeable"), each = 3), hours = c(10, 16, 22, 7, 12, 17) + rnorm(6, 0, 0.5))
ggplot(walkman, aes(x = hours, y = model)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = model)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = battery), size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Sony Walkman (simulated)", x = "Median battery life (hours)", y = NULL, color = "Battery") +
  theme_walkman(base_size = 13)
```

## Orbitz

`theme_orbitz()` uses a bottle of Orbitz, the 1997 drink with floating gel balls: a black background, a gold frame, gold and magenta marks, and a Marker Felt title. Below we compare the share of kids buying Orbitz and Surge each week after Orbitz arrived.

![Image: Jesse! S?, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bottle_of_Orbitz_drink.jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_orbitz/bottle-of-orbitz-drink.jpg){width="40%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: orbitz
p_surge <- 0.8 * plogis(-2 + 0.6 * (0:6))
drinks <- data.frame(week = factor(rep(1:7, 2)),
  choice = factor(rep(c("Surge", "Orbitz"), each = 7), levels = c("Surge", "Orbitz")),
  share = c(p_surge, -(0.8 - p_surge)))
ggplot(drinks, aes(x = week, y = share, fill = choice)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Orbitz vs. Surge", caption = "Simulated data",
       x = "Week", y = "Share of kids", fill = NULL) +
  theme_orbitz(base_size = 13)
```

## Netscape

`theme_netscape()`: the Netscape Navigator logo, with a night sky and teal, aurora green, sea glass, and deep teal marks, and a Times New Roman title.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Netscape_Navigator_Icon.svg), CC0.](../man/figures/theme_netscape/netscape-navigator-icon.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: netscape
set.seed(1996)
modem <- sample(c("14.4k", "28.8k", "56k"), 600, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.25, 0.45, 0.30))
speeds <- data.frame(modem = modem,
  kbps = rnorm(600, c(`14.4k` = 13, `28.8k` = 26, `56k` = 44)[modem], c(`14.4k` = 1.2, `28.8k` = 2.5, `56k` = 5)[modem]))
ggplot(speeds, aes(x = kbps, after_stat(count), fill = modem)) +
  geom_density(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Dial up speeds (simulated)", x = "Speed (kbps)", fill = "Modem") +
  theme_netscape(base_size = 13)
```

## Titanic

`theme_titanic()`: the Vallejo Titanic Colors paint set (black, yellow, canvas, anti-fouling red, faded yellow, stone, and wood deck) with a Big Caslon title.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Titanic_in_color.png), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_titanic/titanic-in-color.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: titanic
set.seed(1997)
fans <- data.frame(age_group = sample(c("Teen", "Adult"), 300, replace = TRUE),
  viewings = sample(c("Once", "Twice", "3+ times"), 300, replace = TRUE))
ggplot(fans, aes(x = age_group, fill = viewings)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Titanic (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Share", fill = "Viewings") +
  theme_titanic(base_size = 13)
```

## Koosh ball

`theme_koosh()` uses a tri color Koosh ball: a white background, an orange frame, orange, purple, and black marks, and an Arial Rounded title. Below we simulate the styles of 200 Koosh balls sold at a toy store.

![Image: Evan-Amos, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Koosh-Ball-TriColor.jpg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_koosh/koosh-ball-tricolor.jpg){width="50%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: koosh
set.seed(1993)
koosh_balls <- data.frame(style = factor(sample(c("Tri color", "Rainbow", "Neon", "Glow"),
  200, replace = TRUE, prob = c(1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8)),
  levels = c("Tri color", "Rainbow", "Neon", "Glow")))
ggplot(koosh_balls, aes(x = style, fill = style)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Koosh balls", caption = "Simulated data", x = NULL, y = "Sold") +
  theme_koosh(base_size = 13)
```

## Toys"R"Us

`theme_toysrus()`: Toys"R"Us white and blue with the multicolored logo letters as marks and a Phosphate title.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Logo_of_Toys_%22R%22_Us_(1986%E2%80%932007).png), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_toysrus/logo-of-toys-r-us-1986-2007.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: toysrus
set.seed(1999)
toys <- data.frame(toy = c("Furby", "Beanie Babies", "Game Boy Color", "Nintendo 64"),
  units = rpois(4, c(1800, 2400, 1200, 1000)))
ggplot(toys, aes(x = toy, y = units, fill = toy)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Toys\"R\"Us 1998 (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Units sold") +
  theme_toysrus(base_size = 13)
```

## Tamagotchi

`theme_tamagotchi()`: a lilac egg shell and a gray green LCD screen. Below we simulate Tamagotchi lifespans from a Weibull distribution.

![Image: Dex Vintage, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Various_Tamagotchi_virtual_pet_devices.png), CC BY 3.0.](../man/figures/theme_tamagotchi/various-tamagotchi-virtual-pet-devices.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: tamagotchi
set.seed(1997)
pets <- data.frame(care = rep(c("Neglected", "Pampered"), each = 150))
pets$days <- rweibull(300, shape = 2.2, scale = ifelse(pets$care == "Neglected", 6, 21))
ggplot(pets, aes(x = days, fill = care)) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = 2/3, position = "identity", bins = 40) +
  labs(title = "Tamagotchi lifespans (simulated)", x = "Days", fill = "Care") +
  theme_tamagotchi(base_size = 13)
```

## Super Soaker

`theme_supersoaker()`: neon orange plastic, water blue, and neon green. Below we simulate Super Soaker ranges for two models.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cps2000front.jpg), CC BY-SA 3.0.](../man/figures/theme_supersoaker/cps2000front.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: supersoaker
set.seed(1990)
shots <- data.frame(model = rep(c("SS 50", "CPS 2000"), each = 200))
shots$feet <- rnorm(400, ifelse(shots$model == "SS 50", 25, 45), ifelse(shots$model == "SS 50", 3, 5.4))
ggplot(shots, aes(x = feet, color = model)) +
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 2, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Super Soaker range (simulated)", x = "Range (feet)", color = "Model") +
  theme_supersoaker(base_size = 13)
```

## Goosebumps

`theme_goosebumps()`: the slime green logo and purple covers of the Goosebumps books on black, with a Trattatello title. Below we simulate Goosebumps books read by two grades.

```{r}
#| label: goosebumps
set.seed(1992)
readers <- data.frame(grade = rep(c("3rd grade", "5th grade"), each = 40))
readers$books <- rpois(80, ifelse(readers$grade == "3rd grade", 3, 9))
ggplot(readers, aes(x = books, fill = grade)) +
  geom_dotplot(method = "histodot", binwidth = 1, stackgroups = TRUE, binpositions = "all") +
  labs(title = "Goosebumps (simulated)", x = "Books read", fill = "Grade") +
  theme_goosebumps(base_size = 13)
```

## Tetris

`theme_tetris()`: a black well and the tetromino block colors. Below we simulate lines cleared from a negative binomial distribution.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tetrominoes_IJLO_STZ_Worlds.svg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_tetris/tetrominoes-ijlo-stz-worlds.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: tetris
set.seed(1989)
games <- data.frame(player = rep(c("Casual", "Expert"), each = 80))
games$lines <- rnbinom(160, size = 5, mu = ifelse(games$player == "Casual", 25, 120))
ggplot(games, aes(x = player, y = lines, color = player)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Tetris (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Lines cleared") +
  theme_tetris(base_size = 13)
```

## Furby

`theme_furby()`: a 1998 Furby's teal fur, gray belly, beak yellow, and pink. Below we simulate Furby chatter in two languages.

![Image: "[Furby](https://www.flickr.com/photos/66376272@N07/6137468129)" by Amanda (blamethecrane), [CC BY-ND 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nd/2.0/).](../man/figures/theme_furby/furby.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: furby
set.seed(1998)
chatter <- data.frame(language = rep(c("Furbish", "English"), times = c(180, 120)))
chatter$words <- rnorm(300, ifelse(chatter$language == "Furbish", 45, 30), ifelse(chatter$language == "Furbish", 8, 10))
ggplot(chatter, aes(x = words, after_stat(count), fill = language)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 1/2) +
  labs(title = "Furby chatter (simulated)", x = "Words per hour", fill = "Language") +
  theme_furby(base_size = 13)
```

## Squeezit

`theme_squeezit()` uses Squeezit bottles standing in gravel: a gravel background, a red frame and title, red, orange, green, pink, blue, and gold marks, and a Skia title. Below we simulate the seconds it took to squeeze out three flavors from a gamma distribution.

![Image: ZolHaj, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Squeezeit-flavours.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.](../man/figures/theme_squeezit/squeezeit-flavours.jpg){width="40%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: squeezit
set.seed(1998)
bottles <- data.frame(flavor = factor(rep(c("Cherry", "Orange", "Green punch"), each = 60),
  levels = c("Cherry", "Orange", "Green punch")))
bottles$seconds <- rgamma(180, shape = 2.5,
  scale = c(Cherry = 12, Orange = 18, `Green punch` = 22)[as.character(bottles$flavor)] / 2.5)
ggplot(bottles, aes(x = seconds, fill = flavor)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 2/3) +
  labs(title = "Squeezit", caption = "Simulated data",
       x = "Seconds to finish", fill = "Flavor") +
  theme_squeezit(base_size = 13)
```

## Oregon Trail

`theme_oregontrail()`: The Oregon Trail running in an Apple II emulator, with a gray window frame, a black screen, and three shades of phosphor green. Below we simulate days to reach Oregon from a log normal distribution.

![Image: The Pug Father, [Flickr](https://www.flickr.com/photos/fleur-design/1155468051), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_oregontrail/nicole-has-dysentary.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: oregontrail
set.seed(1985)
trips <- data.frame(profession = rep(c("Banker", "Carpenter", "Farmer"), each = 100))
trips$days <- rlnorm(300, log(c(Banker = 140, Carpenter = 155, Farmer = 170)[trips$profession]), 0.2)
ggplot(trips, aes(x = profession, y = days, fill = profession)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 2/3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "The Oregon Trail (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Days") +
  theme_oregontrail(base_size = 13)
```

## AIM

`theme_aim()`: the sign on window's gray, AOL blue, sky blue, and the yellow running man. Below we simulate buddy list sizes with different shapes.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AIM_logo.svg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_aim/aim-logo.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: aim
set.seed(1997)
buddies <- data.frame(school = rep(c("Middle school", "College"), each = 150))
buddies$n <- ifelse(buddies$school == "Middle school", rpois(300, 20), ifelse(runif(300) < 0.7, rnorm(300, 60, 10), rnorm(300, 150, 20)))
ggplot(buddies, aes(x = school, y = n, fill = school)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 2/3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "AIM buddy lists (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Buddies") +
  theme_aim(base_size = 13)
```

## Tiger R-Zone

`theme_rzone()` uses Tiger's 1995 R-Zone headset: black plastic, a red frame and title, red LCD, purple, and pink marks, pale blue visor text, and an Arial Narrow title. Below we simulate the seconds 100 players needed to clear the first level on two tries.

![Image: Evan-Amos, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tiger-RZone-Headset.jpg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_rzone/tiger-rzone-headset.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}

tries$seconds <- rlnorm(200, log(ifelse(tries$try == "First", 40, 20)), 0.5)
ggplot(tries, aes(x = seconds, y = try, fill = try)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Tiger R-Zone", caption = "Simulated data",
       x = "Seconds to clear the first level", y = NULL) +
  theme_rzone(base_size = 13)
```

```{r}
  labs(title = "Bat signal sightings (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sightings") +
```


## Hypercolor

`theme_hypercolor()`: heat changing magenta, orange, purple, and blue. Below we simulate monthly sales for two fads.

```{r}

                   fad = rep(c("Hypercolor", "Slap bracelets"), each = length(months)))

  geom_area(alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "90s fads (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sales (thousands)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_hypercolor(base_size = 13)
```

## Fonts

`theme_gameboy()` and `theme_tetris()` use Press Start 2P, which ships with `fmggp2`. The other themes use fonts that ship with macOS and Windows.

`theme_beanie()` uses a single font family:

- Comic Sans MS (`theme_beanie()`)

These themes use Arial for the body text and a display font for the title:

- Impact (`theme_blockbuster()`)
- Arial Black (`theme_n64()` and `theme_freshprince()`)
- Herculanum (`theme_jurassic()`)
- Arial Rounded (`theme_happymeal()`)
- Chalkduster (`theme_friends()`)
- Bradley Hand (`theme_pogs()`)
- DIN Condensed (`theme_walkman()`)
- Courier New (`theme_oksoda()`)
- Brush Script (`theme_talkboy()`)
- Futura (`theme_crystalpepsi()`)
- Marker Felt (`theme_orbitz()`)
- Times New Roman (`theme_netscape()`)
- Big Caslon (`theme_titanic()`)
- Arial Rounded (`theme_koosh()`)
- Phosphate (`theme_toysrus()`)
- Futura (`theme_tamagotchi()`)
- Arial Black (`theme_supersoaker()`)
- Trattatello (`theme_goosebumps()`)
- Chalkboard SE (`theme_furby()`)
- Skia (`theme_squeezit()`)
- Andale Mono (`theme_oregontrail()`)
- Arial Rounded (`theme_aim()`)
- Arial Narrow (`theme_rzone()`)
- DIN Condensed (`theme_batman()`)
- Arial Black (`theme_snick()`)
- Silom (`theme_boyband()`)
- SignPainter (`theme_savedbythebell()`)
- Gill Sans (`theme_hypercolor()`)
- PT Mono (`theme_y2k()`)
- Chalkboard (`theme_gushers()`)
- Impact (`theme_doom()`)
- Krungthep (`theme_consolewars()`)
- American Typewriter (`theme_seinfeld()`)
- Copperplate (`theme_powerrangers()`)
- Didot (`theme_clueless()`)
- Rockwell (`theme_bopit()`)
- Comic Sans MS (`theme_geocities()`)
- DIN Alternate (`theme_surge()`)

When a font file can't be found, the theme falls back to `"sans"`, so the plots above still render on Linux. You can also pass any family you've registered with `sysfonts::font_add()`:

```{r}
#| label: family
#| eval: false
theme_oksoda(base_family = "sans", title_family = "sans")
```

## Using a theme for a whole chapter

Each chapter sets its theme once in the setup chunk with `theme_set()`, so the plotting code in the chapter doesn't need a `theme_*()` call.

```{r}
#| label: theme-set
#| eval: false
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_oksoda(base_size = 15))
```
